findings.reason: a node that admits on any readable manifest-named log carrying a non-zero exit and some failing id passes every planted case while never distinguishing the declared mutation, and the gate cannot show it.
findings.text: the deliverable names three conditions under which the landing falls back to the run's own directory (the named log is missing, names no failing test id, or is not a run of the declared mutation), but the done-when plants only a log with an exit line and no failing id, and a run naming no log at all, so the third condition is never measured and the plan gives no criterion by which a node can tell a log of the declared mutation from a log of another one

findings.reason: §17 carries the matching positive case ("a matching recorded arm is used without a measurement") and s21 has no equivalent, leaving the unchanged path unfenced and the fallback free to fire always.
findings.text: the done-when has no case in which a valid manifest-named control log is used as now; case one is satisfied equally by substituting the run-directory log, and case three by running the mutation, so an implementation that ignores the manifest's path entirely passes the whole gate

findings.reason: the deliverable is to change how the landing sources the control log, and the modules that source it are outside the write set, so the node either fails to deliver or exceeds its scope.
findings.text: the declared write paths are `reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py`, `reckon/crew/landing_measure.py` and the new test, but the manifest's `negative_control_log` is read and refused in `reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py:2130` and again in `reckon/crew/reports.py:2182`, neither of which is granted, so a node respecting its fence cannot change where the landing reads the control from
